text.overview: From the Fourmile Creek side, follow the old mining road past two old mines (Dauntless, Hilltop) to the 13,140-ft col with Mount Sheridan, then walk about a mile northeast up the crest on a well-worn path to the long, flat top.

text.description: Ridge walk usually combined with American and Jones peaks.
Tundra and talus ridge in the Collegiate Peaks, often combined with Ice Mountain.
Remote tundra walk reached by a rough road near Creede; adds a few miles if the road is not driven.
Reached only across private ranch land with a permit; it is a ridge walk usually done after Culebra Peak.
Long grassy ridge in the remote eastern San Juans; mileage depends heavily on how far a vehicle can drive up the Stewart Creek road.
Steep couloir and west-face scrambling reached from the Maroon Lake area; very loose rock makes rockfall a serious hazard, so helmets and small parties matter.
Remote Grenadier peak reached from Vestal Basin with exposed ridge climbing.
Talus slope above Chicago Basin, normally combined with Pigeon Peak.
Remote ridge hike from the Silver Creek road near Redcloud.
Tundra ridge reached by a rough 4x4 road near Redcloud; also climbed in a combo with its neighbor.

text.overview: The usual way up the peak. You reach the crest around 13,800 ft just beyond a notable notch, after which a track skirts the ridge's west flank with a couple of scrambly spots before arriving at a wide summit plateau.

text.description: Open ridge and loose talus above Telluride's Ophir area with a short final scramble.

text.overview: A scrambling finish: from Twin Lakes basin you head east and cut up onto the ridge, with Peak Eighteen sitting at the ridge's western end.
